sentences.text: She found out about the rest of the building by accident, in the lift, from Mr Petrov on the sixth floor, who was about eighty and who had a way of starting conversations in the middle.
He said: "You have been standing on the fourth landing." Nadia said she had been taking the recycling down.
"For twenty minutes.
On Tuesday." The lift went past two.
"It is all right.
I have also stood there." She said nothing at all.
The lift in Block C is slow and there are six floors and there is nowhere to look.
"Konstantin," said Mr Petrov.
"Not Kostya.
Not Kolya.
Konstantin, the whole thing, which nobody has said in this country since my mother died in 1994." The lift stopped.
"It gets it right, also.
The stress in the correct place.
Which the bank does not." She rode up to six with him and then down to four and then up to six again, because he was talking.
What she found out over that week, and over the following month, by asking about fourteen people in a building of forty-four flats, was this.
The owl said everybody's.

Not everybody heard it — you had to be on a landing at night, and most people are not on landings at night, and a great many of the ones who are had put it down to a bird making a noise that sounded a bit like something.
But the ones who had heard it properly had all heard the same category of thing: the name that is not the one on the buzzer.
Mrs Óspina on two, who had been Mercedes Alejandra for sixty-one years and had been Mrs Óspina for thirty of them.

A boy in the year above Nadia at school whose family had been in the country for four generations and whose middle name was his great-grandfather's and was, he said, "properly embarrassing," and who had heard it twice and told nobody until Nadia asked him directly in a corridor.
The building's caretaker, who said he did not believe in any of it and then, after a pause of about eight seconds, said his was Ferenc.
There were two people who had heard nothing and were annoyed about it.

And there was Mrs Deniz on five, who had heard it, and who had come out onto the landing with a broom, and who had been extremely clear with Nadia that she considered the whole thing an intrusion and that a name is private property and that she had written to the committee about the window.
Nadia thought about that one for a long time afterwards, because Mrs Deniz was not wrong.
It is an intrusion.
Something outside a window in the dark knows a thing about you that you have gone to considerable trouble to keep, and it says it out loud without being asked.
It only stops being an intrusion if you happen to be glad, and there is no version of the arrangement in which the owl checks first.
